newsitem.title: UK: UK retail sales show slight pickup in January - BRC.
newsitem.headline: UK retail sales show slight pickup in January - BRC.

text.p: Retail sales in Britain showed a slight pickup in value in January, with a good performance in most non-food sectors offsetting a weaker picture in food and drink, the British Retail Consortium (BRC) said.
Its retail sales monitor showed an annual increase of 4.9 percent in the like-for-like value of retail sales, up from 4.3 percent in December.

"However, the underlying rate of increase in the value of retail sales, as measured by the average for the last three months, has fallen back to 4.7 percent, the lowest three-month growth rate recorded by the BRC since last spring," the organisation said.

Andrew Higginson, chairman of the BRC economic affairs committee, said the latest figures pointed to a healthy picture for the economy as a whole, with the value of retail sales stabilising at a growth rate just below five percent.

"When combined with an increase of only 1.8 percent in the price of retail goods recorded in December, a trend that we foresee continuing in January, the overall outlook points towards healhty growth in consumer demand, with low inflation," he said.

BRC chief economic adviser Andrew Sentance said the figures were reassuring, suggesting that consumer spending would continue to support economic growth in the first half of 1997, and the short-term economic outlook was very favourable.
"Retail spending is not growing so strongly that it poses an inflatiomnary threat," he said.

The latest survey, covering the period from January 5 to February 1, showed a tough month for food retailing. Falling inflation meant the year on year rise in food sales by value was marginally lower in January than was achieved in December.
A relatively strong performance in non-food was seen in sectors ranging from clothing to medicines and do-it-yourself.
"The tourist trade in London was hit by the stronger pound and fewer purchases by visitors from abroad, particularly from the Far East," the BRC said.
